subject: Solvix dedicated pool: throughput profiles, SLO fit, and recommended commit
messages:
From: Sara Molina <sara.molina@solvix.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solvix.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning — peak profile and SLA targets

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing to finalize the Dedicated commitment for our GenAI assistant and need a concrete sizing recommendation tied to our SLOs so procurement can sign off. Quick summary of our expected workload:
- Model: redwood-v2-13B (quality target)
- Average response length: ~120 tokens (completion only)
- Active user concurrency window (peak): 1100 concurrent sessions, average 1.5 requests/sec/user during peak bursts
- Target P95 end-to-end response latency: <= 750 ms for a 120-token completion
- Expected sustained tokens/sec (business hours, peak): ~1,800 tokens/sec
- Spike / holiday peak (short bursts): up to ~4,500 tokens/sec for 5–10 minutes

Can you send a simple mapping: tokens/sec requirement -> GPUs needed (baseline, spike) and recommended safety/headroom assumptions? Procurement also wants to see upgrade/burst options (commit vs burst to handle the 4.5k spikes).

If useful I've attached our usage histogram and a sample traffic day.

Cheers,
Sara
Sara Molina
Head of Product
Solvix AI

Attachment: solvix_usage_histogram.csv (referenced)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Molina <sara.molina@solvix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — peak profile and SLA targets

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear numbers and the histogram. I ran a short sizing pass with the runtime team and attached a spreadsheet with the calculations (solvix_compute_model_v1.xlsx). High-level recommendation below; see the sheet for per-scenario math.

Summary assumptions we used (config aligned to the demo):
- Model: rw_v2_13B, q4f16 quantized runtime
- Hardware: A100 80GB equivalence (our A100 slot performance model)
- Avg completion length: 120 tokens; context length accounted for in KV cache warm path
- Median batch depth during peak: 6–8 requests (we size for batch=8 in steady bursts)
- P95 latency target: <= 750 ms for the 120-token completion (end-to-end generation)

Measured throughput (internal profiling, batching=8, q4f16):
- Per-A100 effective max throughput (peak config): ~1,200 tokens/sec
- Safe operating capacity (apply 30% headroom for latency SLO and multi-tenant noise): 840 tokens/sec per GPU

Sizing math (simple):
- Sustained peak requirement: 1,800 t/s -> 1,800 / 840 = 2.14 -> round up to 3 GPUs
- Short spikes to 4,500 t/s -> 4,500 / 840 = 5.36 -> round up to 6 GPUs

Recommendation (deal-friendly):
- Commit: 4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (covers sustained with some breathing room and keeps monthly commit modest)
- Autoscale burst: allow up to 6 GPUs for short spike windows (5–10 min); billing for burst hours beyond baseline is metered
- Operational safeguards: auto-warm KV cache on scale-up, rotate canary traffic, and pre-warm model shards prior to known marketing spikes

Why 4 commit? It balances cost and risk: reserves cover most steady state (3 required), the 4th GPU cuts the effective load per unit and reduces frequency of autoscale events. The burst to 6 keeps your SLO for short windows. If Solvix prefers strict p95 guarantees for unbounded spikes we’d recommend committing 6, but that materially increases monthly unit costs.

Notes on cost/quality tradeoffs and fallback:
- We can route low-importance traffic to rw_v2_7B (per-GPU throughput ~2,000 t/s in q4f16), preserving quality traffic on 13B. This hybrid routing reduces commit needs but adds routing complexity.
- Quantization and prefix caching reduce sustained GPU needs by ~15–25% in our tests; we captured a few sample scenarios in the sheet.

Next steps: Ben will include an ops play (scale triggers + cooldowns) and Jonas will draft the SLA language for the DocuSign. If that plan looks OK we can draft the order form and a DocuSign for your procurement team.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: solvix_compute_model_v1.xlsx (detailed math)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sara Molina <sara.molina@solvix.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning — peak profile and SLA targets

Sara / team — quick ops note from the runtime side:

If you go with the commit=4, burst=6 pattern Hannah suggested, here's an ops checklist we recommend shipping in the SOW so the SLA holds during spikes:
- Autoscale trigger: scale-up when 1-min moving average > 75% of per-GPU safe capacity (i.e., > 630 t/s aggregate per GPU).
- Scale cooldown: 10 minutes for scale-down to avoid flapping during composite bursts.
- KV cache warm policy: pre-warm using sample request set for the top 10% of traffic paths immediately after scale-up. Warm time we measured ~45–120s depending on model cache hit patterns.
- Fallback routing: low-priority inference traffic -> rw_v2_7B; implement weighted routing during sustained >30% above baseline.
- Canary window: first 3% of burst traffic goes to new replicas for 2 minutes before full routing.

Operational impact on headroom math: pre-warming reduces the effective warm-up latency and improves immediate P95 by ~150–200 ms on average in our tests; we included that delta in the attached SLA doc.

I'll add a short paragraph to the SOW that spells out those triggers and responsibilities (Redwood ops vs Solvix on-call).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will include ops play excerpt in final SOW)

1) Can you add explicit language around expected warm-up time in the SLA (we want assurance on pre-warm and a short credit if warm-up exceeds 5 minutes for scheduled bursts)?
2) Please include a DocuSign-ready order form with the pricing delta between commit=4 vs commit=6 (monthly commit and per-hour burst pricing).

Once we have that I'll route to Procurement. Can you also include the Drive link with the workbook and the final SLA?

Appreciate the fast turn.

Sara
